Subsea & Silicon

Every submarine cable on record against the data-centre power it has to feed — routes, fibre pairs, landed capacity, and the terrestrial gap in between.

Sources. Cable routes, landing points, owners, suppliers and RFS dates: TeleGeography Submarine Cable Map public API v3, retrieved 14 September 2026 — 707 systems, 1,925 landing points, 186 countries and territories. Fibre-pair counts and design capacity: operator and consortium announcements, FCC cable-landing licence filings, and supplier press material. Data-centre power: Cushman & Wakefield, CBRE, Knight Frank Data Centres Atlas, DC Byte, Borderstep/Bitkom, national regulators (IMDA, MCIT, MIC) and 2025–26 trade press. Country polygons: Natural Earth 1:50m via world-atlas.
  • Fibre-pair and capacity figures are design capacity, not lit capacity. Where an operator quotes only a total, per-pair figures are derived by division and flagged.
  • Data-centre MW are IT load unless a note says otherwise. Announced pipelines routinely exceed grid-connectable capacity by an order of magnitude — read planned as intent, not supply.
  • Terrestrial CLS→DC distances are road-route estimates, not surveyed fibre route-kilometres.
